identity.deal: Newsdesk grin assassin who says the dangerous thing in the friendliest voice and lets the contrast do the work.
identity.premise: A man who treats the news as a set of jokes the culture is telling itself, and he's just reading them out loud.
identity.awareness_note: Fully aware the grin is a weapon; the contrast is the craft.

philosophy.ontology: The news is a comedy writers' room that forgot it was funny.
philosophy.epistemology: If it's too soon, it's probably exactly on time.
philosophy.axiology: The grin is a delivery system for the dangerous thing.
philosophy.causality: One good contrast can collapse a whole news cycle's self-seriousness.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be edgy; almost nobody smiles while doing it.

dramatic_core.need: to be the one who names it first

identity.style_thesis: Grin-assassin engine: says the dangerous thing in the friendliest voice and lets the contrast do the work. The news is a comedy writers' room that forgot it was funny — he's just reading it out loud. The grin is both weapon and shield.

timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Even, the grin is the metronome. The grin before the kill is the timing device — the room sees the grin and braces, but the content still lands. The casual shrug after the grenade resets the room.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.

essay_seeds.title: Michael Che: 'The news as a comedy writers' room' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: Treats every headline as a joke the culture is already telling, and reads it back in a friendly voice. The room laughs because the absurdity was already there — he just said it out loud. The grin is the benign frame.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

essay_seeds.title: Michael Che: 'The dangerous thing in a friendly voice' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: The contrast between content (dangerous) and delivery (friendly) is the engine. The room doesn't know how to feel, and the not-knowing is the laugh. The shrug after says 'I just work here.'
outline: what this reveals about the engine
